title: Unsupervised clustering links deep-earthquake scaling to hydration differences among northwest Pacific slabs
summary: K-means clustering of Japan Meteorological Agency deep-earthquake catalogs separated the northwest Pacific slab segments; Gutenberg–Richter analysis found a magnitude 3.7–3.8 kink in Honshu and Izu seismicity, with b values falling from about 1.4–1.7 to 0.6–0.7. The authors infer that small-event excess and an approximately kilometre-scale metastable-olivine-wedge rim may reflect deep hydration and enhanced transformational faulting.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine-learning clustering (K-means, checked against spectral clustering and Gaussian mixture models)
organization: Michigan State University; Freie Universität Berlin; Université d’Orléans–CNRS; University of California, Los Angeles; Yale University

evidence.tested: K-means clustering of Japan Meteorological Agency deep-earthquake catalogs separated the northwest Pacific slab segments; Gutenberg–Richter analysis found a magnitude 3.7–3.8 kink in Honshu and Izu seismicity, with b values falling from about 1.4–1.7 to 0.6–0.7.
evidence.unknown: The observed b-value kink is a statistical result. Hydrous defects and an approximately 1 km unstable wedge rim are the authors’ geodynamic interpretation, not direct water-content measurements; the authors discuss magnitude-detection and model assumptions.
evidence.ai_role: Clustered deep-earthquake distributions into four slab segments, enabling region-specific b-value analyses that exposed the Honshu/Izu magnitude kink and its proposed relation to slab hydration.
